title: Mixed listening
goal: Understand short announcements, messages and conversations, including everyday Québec French, by listening for key words.

example.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais en fin de semaine ?
example.en: What are you doing this weekend?

items.note: In Québec, it means OK, no problem, not “that's right”.
In France, le dîner is the evening meal and lunch is le déjeuner.
In France, the evening meal is le dîner.

example.fr: Le magasin va fermer dans dix minutes.
example.en: The store is going to close in ten minutes.

accept: Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
Parlez plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.

steps.title: Four things you might hear this week
steps.intro: Read the question under each recording **before** you listen. Then listen once without the transcript.

blocks.title: At the bus stop
blocks.context: An announcement at a bus terminal.
blocks.fr: Mesdames et messieurs, attention, s'il vous plaît. Le bus numéro 80 est en retard de dix minutes. Nous sommes désolés. Merci de votre patience.
blocks.en: Ladies and gentlemen, attention, please. Bus number 80 is ten minutes late. We are sorry. Thank you for your patience.

blocks.prompt: What is the problem with bus 80?
blocks.explain: Key words: [[en retard]] (late) and [[dix minutes]]. You don't need [[mesdames et messieurs]] to answer.

blocks.title: Plans for the weekend
blocks.context: Lucie, from Montréal, talks to her friend Raj. Listen for the day, the place and the time.
blocks.fr:
— Salut Raj ! Qu'est-ce que tu fais en fin de semaine ?
— Samedi, je travaille. Mais dimanche, je suis libre.
— Super ! On va au marché Jean-Talon dimanche matin ? Après, on peut dîner chez moi.
— Dîner ? Le soir ?
— Mais non ! Ici, le dîner, c'est à midi. Le soir, c'est le souper !
— Ah, d'accord ! C'est correct pour moi. À quelle heure ?
— Vers dix heures, au métro Jean-Talon. J'appelle Mei tantôt : elle adore le marché, elle aussi.
— Parfait. À dimanche !
blocks.en: — Hi Raj! What are you doing this weekend? — On Saturday, I'm working. But on Sunday, I'm free. — Great! Shall we go to the Jean-Talon market on Sunday morning? After that, we can have lunch at my place. — Dinner? In the evening? — No! Here, le dîner is at noon. In the evening, it's le souper! — Oh, OK! That's fine with me. What time? — Around ten, at Jean-Talon metro station. I'm calling Mei later today: she loves the market too. — Perfect. See you Sunday!

blocks.prompt: What are Lucie and Raj going to do on Sunday?
options: Go to the market at 10 a.m., then have lunch at Lucie's
Work in the morning, then have supper
Go to the market on Saturday evening
blocks.explain: [[dimanche matin]], [[vers dix heures]], then [[dîner chez moi]]: in Québec, le dîner is lunch.

blocks.title: A voicemail from the building
blocks.context: Marc-André, the building superintendent, leaves a message for a tenant.
blocks.fr: Bonjour, c'est Marc-André, le concierge de l'immeuble. Le technicien va passer tantôt, vers quatorze heures, pour le chauffage. Vous n'êtes pas à la maison ? C'est correct, j'ai la clé. Bonne fin de semaine !
blocks.en: Hello, it's Marc-André, the building superintendent. The technician is going to come by later today, around 2 p.m., for the heating. You're not at home? That's fine, I have the key. Have a good weekend!

options: The technician is coming today around 2 p.m., and you don't need to be home.
The technician is coming on the weekend, and you must be home.
You need to bring your key to the superintendent at 4 p.m.
blocks.explain: [[tantôt]] = later today, [[quatorze heures]] = 2 p.m., and [[C'est correct, j'ai la clé]] = it's fine, he has the key.

blocks.title: Calling a clinic
blocks.context: Nguyen phones a medical clinic to make an appointment.
blocks.fr:
— Clinique du Parc, bonjour !
— Bonjour, madame. Je voudrais un rendez-vous avec le docteur Roy, s'il vous plaît.
— Oui… Mardi à dix heures quinze, c'est possible ?
— Non, désolé, je travaille le matin. Vous avez un rendez-vous l'après-midi ?
— Jeudi à quinze heures trente ?
— Parfait, merci !
— Votre nom, s'il vous plaît ?
— Nguyen : N, G, U, Y, E, N.
— Merci, monsieur Nguyen. À jeudi !
blocks.en: — Parc Clinic, hello! — Hello. I'd like an appointment with Dr. Roy, please. — Yes… Tuesday at 10:15, is that possible? — No, sorry, I work in the morning. Do you have an appointment in the afternoon? — Thursday at 3:30 p.m.? — Perfect, thank you! — Your name, please? — Nguyen: N, G, U, Y, E, N. — Thank you, Mr. Nguyen. See you Thursday!

blocks.explain: Tuesday morning was the first offer, but he works in the morning. The final answer is [[jeudi à quinze heures trente]]. Listen to the **end** of a conversation: plans often change!

blocks.title: Three listening strategies
blocks.body:
**1. Predict.** Before you listen, read the question and the context. A clinic call? Expect a day, a time and a name. A bus announcement? Expect a number and maybe [[en retard]].

**2. Catch the key words.** Listen for nouns, numbers, days and negatives ([[ne… pas]]). Small words like [[mesdames et messieurs]] or [[merci de votre patience]] are polite noise: let them go.

**3. Don't panic on unknown words.** In the voicemail, maybe you don't know [[chauffage]] (heating). You can still answer *who*, *when* and *what to do*. Keep listening: the next sentence often explains the one before.

And in real life, you can always ask: [[Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?]] or [[Plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.]]

blocks.title: Québec or France? Same idea, different words
head: Québec
France
English
blocks.note: Everyone in Québec understands the France words too. But if you live in Canada, you will **hear** the Québec words every day.

blocks.title: The sound of Québec French
blocks.body:
A few common **tendencies** help you recognize a Québec speaker (not everyone speaks the same way):

- **t and d before i and u** often get a little *s* or *z* sound: [[tu]] sounds like *tsu*, [[dire]] like *dzire*, [[midi]] like *mi-dzi*.
- **Il and ils** often lose the *l* in casual speech: [[il fait froid]] can sound like *i fait froid*.
- **Long vowels**: in words like [[fête]], [[père]] or [[pâte]], the vowel is often held longer than in France, and can glide a little.

This is not “bad French”: it is the normal French of millions of people. You don't need to copy it, but you need to understand it.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais en fin de semaine ?
examples.en: What are you doing this weekend?

blocks.title: Why you understand more than you think
blocks.body:
When you listen, your brain fills gaps using **context**. If you hear *bus*, *numéro 80*, *dix minutes* and *désolés*, you can guess the bus is late even without [[en retard]].

So listen for the **big picture first**, then for details. On exams like the TEF and TCF Canada, you hear each recording once or twice: reading the question first is your best tool.

- **C'est correct ≠ That's correct.** In Québec, it means *it's OK, no problem*. To say *that's right*, use [[C'est ça.]] or [[C'est vrai.]]
- **Dîner at noon.** If a Québec friend invites you to [[dîner]], don't arrive at 7 p.m.!
- **Numbers in the 70s and 90s:** [[soixante-dix]] (70), [[quatre-vingt-dix]] (90). Write the number down as you hear it, one piece at a time.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: These are phrases you'll hear (and say) in Canada. Repeat, then record yourself.

lines.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais en fin de semaine ?
lines.en: What are you doing this weekend?
lines.tip: Qu'est-ce que sounds like one word: kess-kuh.
correct: the final ct is pronounced.
tantôt: a nasal an, then a closed o: tan-to.
plus: the s is silent here.

blocks.fr: Chers clients, le magasin va fermer dans quinze minutes. Merci de passer à la caisse.
blocks.en: Dear customers, the store is going to close in fifteen minutes. Please go to the checkout.
options: Go to the checkout: the store closes soon
Wait: the store opens in fifteen minutes
blocks.explain: [[va fermer]] (futur proche) + [[dans quinze minutes]] = closes soon. [[la caisse]] = the checkout.

blocks.fr: Allô, c'est Amira. Je ne peux pas aller au cours demain. On peut changer la date ?
blocks.en: Hello, it's Amira. I can't go to the class tomorrow. Can we change the date?
options: She can't go tomorrow and wants another date.
She wants to go to the class tomorrow.
She wants to cancel the class forever.
blocks.explain: The negative [[je ne peux pas]] is the key: always listen for [[ne… pas]].

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Read each question first, then listen. You can play the audio again.

blocks.fr: Le train pour Québec arrive à quinze heures quarante.
blocks.en: The train to Québec City arrives at 3:40 p.m.
blocks.explain: [[quinze heures]] = 3 p.m. and [[quarante]] = 40. Don't confuse [[quarante]] (40) and [[quatorze]] (14).

blocks.fr: On va au cinéma en fin de semaine ? C'est correct pour toi ?
blocks.en: Shall we go to the movies this weekend? Is that OK with you?
options: Going to the movies this weekend
blocks.explain: [[en fin de semaine]] = this weekend in Québec; [[C'est correct pour toi ?]] = is that OK for you?

blocks.prompt: Your Québec colleague says: “On dîne ensemble ? À midi ?” What is she proposing?
blocks.explain: In Québec, [[dîner]] is the midday meal. The evening meal is [[le souper]].

blocks.text: — Je suis un peu en retard. — Pas de problème, c'est ___ !
blocks.en: — I'm a bit late. — No problem, that's fine!
blocks.explain: [[C'est correct]] is the Québec way to say *it's OK*. After [[c'est]], the adjective stays masculine.

blocks.fr: Bonjour, ici la pharmacie. Vos médicaments sont prêts. Nous sommes ouverts jusqu'à vingt et une heures.
blocks.en: Hello, this is the pharmacy. Your medication is ready. We're open until 9 p.m.
blocks.prompt: Until what time is the pharmacy open?
blocks.explain: [[vingt et une heures]] = 21 h = 9 p.m. Don't let unknown words like [[médicaments]] stop you: it's a cognate!

accept: Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
Est-ce que vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
blocks.explain: [[pouvoir]] + infinitive: [[vous pouvez répéter]]. Inversion ([[Pouvez-vous]]) is a little more formal.

blocks.prompt: Match the Québec words with their meaning.

blocks.fr: Le rendez-vous est jeudi à quinze heures trente.
accept: Le rendez-vous est jeudi à 15 h 30.
blocks.explain: [[rendez-vous]] has a hyphen and a silent z and s.
[[libre]] = free, not busy. Days take no capital letter in French.

blocks.fr: Salut, c'est Olivier ! Je ne vais pas au match samedi. Je travaille. Désolé !
blocks.en: Hi, it's Olivier! I'm not going to the game on Saturday. I'm working. Sorry!
options: He isn't going to the game because he's working.
He's going to the game after work.
He's working at the game on Saturday.
blocks.explain: [[Je ne vais pas]] = I'm not going. The negative changes everything: listen for [[ne… pas]].

blocks.prompt: Leave a voicemail for a friend in Montréal. Say who you are, suggest a plan for the weekend with a day and a time, ask if it's OK, and say you'll call later today.
checklist: A plan with a place: On va au… / à la… ?
A day and a time (samedi, vers dix heures…)
Say you'll call later: Je t'appelle tantôt (I'll call you later today)
A goodbye: À tantôt ! / Bonne fin de semaine !

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Lucie, c'est Raj ! Tu es libre en fin de semaine ? On va au parc La Fontaine samedi, vers onze heures ? Après, on peut dîner au restaurant. C'est correct pour toi ? Je t'appelle tantôt. À tantôt !
models.en: Hi Lucie, it's Raj! Are you free this weekend? Shall we go to La Fontaine Park on Saturday, around eleven? After that, we can have lunch at a restaurant. Is that OK with you? I'll call you later today. See you later!

summary:
- Predict, catch key words and keep going when you hear unknown words
- Understand announcements, voicemails and short phone calls with days, times and numbers
- Recognize Québec French: [[la fin de semaine]], [[C'est correct]], [[tantôt]], [[le dîner]] and [[le souper]]
